5827974c4e12a41fec269ce5c6be6c7a0682665c: A resort on a human scale, Val Senales focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 42 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly renew their terrain. Its family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. When it comes to snow, Val Senales is in a strong position with its summit at 3212 m: even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold up well until April. The village at 2011 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from mid-December. The cost of a stay at Val Senales is clearly high: €62 for a day pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of quality, but be aware of it before you go. In short, Val Senales doesn't compete with the giants of skiing and doesn't claim to. It's an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.

5846c57a3e57884bb12f615f3f786dc44c6216d3: Auron offers 135 km of well-marked runs, a medium-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever skiing exactly the same thing twice. The 22 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Auron's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Southern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Auron's altitude (1,600 m at the base, 2,450 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow reliability in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The day lift pass at €34 remains reasonable for the quality of the ski area on offer. Counting accommodation, skiing and meals, Auron suits those who want a good week without the final bill knocking them off their chair. In short, Auron keeps its promises: a Southern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
